src/citymap.js:7940 _placeChunkedInstanced does it in ONE draw per (geometry, material, chunk): `makeColor` writes one InstancedBufferAttribute of per-instance colour (mesh.setColorAt(k, c), citymap.js:7975-7979) and a THREE.InstancedMesh wears a material ARRAY over its geometry groups, so N submeshes are N draws but ONE cull record. Both halves ported:
  (a) per-instance colour as a MaterialPropertyBlock VECTOR ARRAY handed to the draw through RenderParams.matProps, which Unity feeds into the shader's GPU-instancing constant buffer against Assets/Shaders/CityKit.shader's UNITY_DEFINE_INSTANCED_PROP(float4, _InstTint). One array per batch, built lazily on a batch's first real draw and cached, so nothing is rebuilt per frame. The tint leaves the batch key and ONE material serves every tint of a kit submesh.
  (b) one Batch per (mesh, chunk) carrying Materials[submesh]; the submesh loop moved INSIDE Submit(), so the DRAW count is untouched while batches/cull records/loop iterations fall by the mesh's submesh count.

SAFETY, because a shader cannot be seen headlessly: KitShader() returns null when Shaders/CityKit.shader is missing OR UnityEditor.ShaderUtil.ShaderHasError says it did not compile, and BuildKitBatches then runs the OLD quantised-material path unchanged. ResolveReport.InstancedTint records which arm ran and EnsureBuilt logs it, so a silent fallback is visible in the bake log rather than invisible on screen. forceQuantisedTint:true is the probe's A/B switch and the only caller that passes it.

NOT TOUCHED, deliberately: the building CHUNK mesh draw path and the imposter LOD. The project memory records those per-group draws as a measured 17 -> 4.4 ms cliff whose far-twin fix regressed old town and was reverted TWICE. This is the kit-instance path only, and Shaders/CityWall.shader is left byte-identical (moving _BaseColor into an instancing cbuffer would make it SRP-Batcher-incompatible, which is why CityKit.shader is a separate file).

TWO DEAD ENDS BEFORE THAT, both worth keeping, because the brief named the first one as the fix and it does not work. (1) Graphics.RenderMeshInstanced<T> with a struct { Matrix4x4 objectToWorld; Vector4 Tint; }: it compiles, and it looks the fields up BY NAME via Marshal.OffsetOf against the built-ins it knows, so the trailing field threw `ArgumentException: Field passed in is not a marshaled member of the type KitInstance` -- from inside LateUpdate, where RenderShotProbe's reflected tick reported it only as `TICKER id=threw type=CityRenderer msg=Exception has been thrown by the target of an invocation` and where FrameBatches/FrameDrawCalls simply stayed 0 because the assignment after Submit() never ran. Every batch/material/instance count in this file was correct and NOT ONE PIXEL was drawn: the canonical 'a probe proves a calculation, not that it is reached' failure. What found it was Editor/Probes/CityKitInstanceProbe.Draw -- ONE real draw of ONE batch, under a REAL graphics device (no -nographics), with `e.InnerException.Message` printed. A headless probe cannot see this at all, because it never issues a draw.
Second cause found by the same probe: `InvalidOperationException: Material needs to enable instancing for use with RenderMeshInstanced` on the facade materials, which only Configure() was setting. enableInstancing is now set where the materials are BUILT, so a batch is drawable the moment it exists and a caller that bypasses Configure cannot see a different bug from the game's.

(2) Renaming that field to `_InstTint` so the by-name lookup would find it: the draw then SUCCEEDED, every count was right, and the tint still never arrived. The pixel test (CityKitInstanceProbe.TintPixels -- three instances tinted RED/GREEN/BLUE, read back out of a RenderTexture) returned 0.800/0.800/0.800 in all three columns. Unity accepts the extra field and drops it. A successful draw proves nothing about the colour.
That near-miss was the whole risk of this pass, because the kit FBX materials are NEUTRAL: the probe reads `matBaseColor=(0.800,0.800,0.800)` on panel_concrete, so the hash tint is not a subtle variation on top of a coloured material -- it is the ONLY colour the kit has. Shipping the silently-dropped tint would have turned 169,004 buildings flat grey while every counter in the bake log read better than before. The property-block route now passes the same pixel test: col0 (0.800,0,0) red, col1 (0,0.800,0) green, col2 (0,0,0.800) blue, plus a yellow material-level control that separates 'the shader never reads _InstTint' from 'the delivery does not arrive'.

note: The per-instance tint shader the batch-key fix needs. Modelled on Shaders/CityWall.shader (same hand-rolled Lambert + Blinn-Phong over GetMainLight/GetAdditionalLight/SampleSH, the house choice PlaneHull.shader and WindFoliage.shader also make; same cotangent-frame TBN so no vertex TANGENT stream is needed, which the kit FBX do not carry; same _MetallicGlossMap R/A modulation; same minimal shadow caster with its OWN #pragma multi_compile_instancing, since ForwardLit's does not carry across a pass). Two deliberate differences: no vertex COLOUR read (the kit FBX have no COLOR stream and a missing stream does not reliably read as white -- the kit's tint is per INSTANCE, which is what the JS does too), and TWO multiplied colours -- _BaseColor per MATERIAL (copied off the source FBX material, where the kit's real h_plaster/a_brick/panel_concrete tones live) times _InstTint per INSTANCE. That multiply is citymap.js's instanceColor semantics (_loadAptKit's 'NO multiplyScalar here' warning against double-dimming) and it is also what lets ONE instance array serve all of a mesh's submeshes: the per-submesh colour stays on the material, so the per-instance payload is the tint alone. Every half literal carries a decimal point (the bare-integer `1h` trap that kept CityWall.shader from ever compiling, and that this same pass found twice more in PlaneHull.shader).

WIRED INTO CityRenderer rather than a new MonoBehaviour: the JS has exactly ONE chunk list (this.chunkMeshes) and ONE per-frame cull loop, and both the building kit and the facade props push into it through the same _placeChunkedInstanced -- so one batch list, one CityCulling sweep and one Submit loop IS the faithful shape. It is also the shape that is REACHED: CityRenderer is already in Assets/Scenes/Game.unity and already runs BuildRich, whereas a second component would have needed a line in Editor/BuildPlayableScene.cs (not this pass's file) and a renderer that is not in Game.unity is one of the three documented ways finished code fails to run.

NO IMPOSTER BAKE: FacadeKitBuilder.Put takes an optional bake Camera and ImposterBaker needs a live render target, which a -nographics batch run has not got. Passing null means no imposter geometry, and the JS's own `put` then passes `lod?.geo ? lod : null` -- NO LOD SWITCH AT ALL, the layer draws out to its own maxDist. Reproduced exactly by setting LodDist = 0 when ImpostorMesh is null; the alternative (LodDist set, impostor null) would HIDE every window past 610 m, which is not what the JS does.

ALL SIX LAYERS DRAW THE PROCEDURAL FALLBACK BOX, and so does the JS: public/models/facade_kit.glb contains exactly ONE node, `ac`, so citymap.js's byVariant(items, 'balcony'|'window') finds no kit entry for any relief variant either and geoOf(v, fallback) returns the same box geometry (citymap.js:6150-6224). Parity, not a shortcut.

NOT INCLUDED: the six FacadeProps layers (AC units, dishes, drainpipes, entrances, parapets, roof props). Those are not in rich.Relief -- BuildRich never builds them; their only producer is CityLoader.BuildFacadePropsForEveryBuilding, which re-derives its per-building inputs from public APIs and documents three approximations, the load-bearing one being pitchedFinal = false ('an OVER-placement on the city's real pitched-roof stock'). Wiring that in would stand roof vents and parapets on pitched cottage roofs: a visible quality regression, not a gap closed. It needs BuildingBuilder.BuildRich to surface its own per-building pitched/contour first (one call in that loop, per CityLoader's own note), and BuildRich is not this pass's file.

PER-LAYER castShadow, which the port had dropped: Submit() hard-coded ShadowCastingMode.On for every batch. citymap.js's `put` passes castShadow: FALSE (citymap.js:6135) for every facade-relief layer, so Batch now carries the flag and the relief does not re-draw 742,561 boxes into the shadow map. The KIT keeps On unconditionally -- it is castShadow: true in the JS. The per-chunk SHADOW_DIST gate (citymap.js:7988-7995, CityCulling.VisChunk.ShOn, 500 m) is still NOT read by Submit: implementing it removes distant kit shadows that are on screen today, which is a look change this pass cannot verify headlessly, so it is reported as an open item instead. The JS's own note beside that gate measured the kits alone at 21M triangles a frame through the depth pass.

note: TWO SHADERS THAT HAD NEVER COMPILED, both found by the first GPU render of the port and both user-visible. PlaneHull.shader: `lerp(1h, ...)` -- a bare-integer half literal is not valid HLSL, the same trap CityWall.shader's header documents. Consequence: HoleSet.Patch swaps every plane skin onto this shader on the first hit, so SHOOTING ANY AEROPLANE TURNED IT SOLID MAGENTA and the _TearInv discard that makes a tear see-through never ran. Two more bare-half literals in the same file (`1h - metallic`, `exp2(10h * smoothness + 1h)`) fixed with it; a repo-wide regex for the pattern now finds none. GlassGlint.shader: `(right * IN.positionOS.x + up * IN.positionOS.y) * scale.xy` is float3 * float2 -- each view axis is now scaled by its own component, so the billboard glint can draw at all. These are 0-line defect fixes in two files; the port units that claim the JS behind them are unchanged.
